title: Quarterly reset station — briefing & runbook (Q3→Q4 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This working brief is a compact runbook for the company-wide quarterly reset workshop and the follow-on town/townless communication cycle. Goal is to align exec decisions, draft OKR reset proposals, and produce the one-page comms + slide deck for the company meeting. This is intentionally informal — living doc for rapid edits during the week of Q3->Q4 planning.

Audience:
- Execs: quick decision inputs
- People leads: headcount, org changes
- Product & Eng leaders: roadmap cadence & rollouts
- All-hands organizers and comms team

Guiding constraints (short):
- Keep company-level OKR changes to 2 big shifts max (reduce cognitive load)
- Preserve commitments that affect customer SLAs or paid contracts unless explicitly renegotiated
- Headcount asks must include: role, impact, ramp plan, and cost estimate

Quick agenda (reset week):
Day 0 (pre-read distributed): key metrics + friction map (2 pages)
Day 1: Exec alignment (top 3 tradeoffs, proposed OKR pivots) — 90m
Day 2: Cross-functional breakout (product x eng x go-to-market) — 120m
Day 3: Decision synthesis & slide drafting — 60m
Day 4: Final approvals + comms rehearsal — 45m

Running the Exec Alignment (playbook):
- Prep: each exec brings a 6-slide micro-brief (metrics, ask, risk, fallback)
- Timebox: 6 minutes per leader, 1 minute for clarifying q, then dot-vote
- Decision framing: explicit options (A/B/C) and the operational owner for each option

Narrative script for the company update (one-paragraph):
"We shipped dense improvements to inference runtime and reduced median gen latency by 23% this quarter while maintaining customer experience. As we prepare for the next phase, we will focus on predictable, cost-efficient serving: consolidate model catalog defaults, invest in Dedicated capacity automations, and expand Private deployment integrations for regulated accounts. The immediate changes are targeted to reduce unit cost and increase uptime for enterprise workloads — details and team owners are below."

OKR reset proposals (drafts — pick one set):
Option A — Focused efficiency (recommended)
- Company OKR: Reduce per-token serving cost by 18% by EOY through batching, quantization, and routing policies
- Why: immediate margin impact for hosted API customers; clear engineering workstreams
- Risks: small regressions in tail-latency if batching thresholds miscalibrate

Option B — Platform expansion
- Company OKR: Ship Redwood Private 2.0 baseline for two regulated vertical customers + 99.9% Uptime SLA for Dedicated tiers
- Why: revenue expansion and higher ARR per account
- Risks: heavier ops burden and longer sales cycles

Option C — Growth-first
- Company OKR: Prioritize new product integrations (VectorDB partners, developer SDKs) to increase self-serve conversion by 30%
- Why: PLG funnel optimization
- Risks: distracts from unit economics, higher infra spend for small experiments

Metrics to surface in exec meeting (single-line each):
- Revenue run-rate & committed ARR (YTD vs target)
- Hosting unit cost per 1M tokens (spot vs reserved)
- Median/95th latency for gen and embeddings (prod traffic)
- Incident count & mean-time-to-detect (MTTD) this quarter
- Developer signups and API key activation rate

Decision log (template lines — fill during workshop):
- [DATE] Decision: <short statement> | Choosen option: A/B/C | Owner: <name> | Next step: <action> | Deadline: <date>

Comms plan (post-decision):
- Internal: exec email + leadership one-pager by EOD Day 4 (owner: Communications)
- All-hands: 20-min slot + 2 breakout Q&A rooms (owner: People Ops)
- Customer-facing blog / product update: coordinate w/marketing + legal for any capability announcements

Slide deck outline (for town meeting):
- Cover: "Quarterly Reset — Where we are and where we go"
- Topline metrics (1 slide)
- What changed this quarter (2 slides)
- Why this reset matters (1 slide)
- The choices we considered (1 slide)
- Our decision and what it means for each org (3 slides, org-specific)
- Roadmap milestones & key dates (1 slide)
- Q&A / next steps (1 slide)

Open questions / needles to thread (notes-to-self):
- Legal: any contract implications for changing Dedicated SLAs? (Aisha to confirm)
- Sales: will existing customers push back on model pinning defaults? (Elena to surface top 5 accounts)
- Eng: can runtime team commit to the 18% cost reduction without adding >2 FTEs? (Kai to estimate)

Action items (initial):
- Aisha: contract impact map + recommendation (due: 2026-07-25)
- Kai: rough engineering plan for batching/quantization experiments (due: 2026-07-24)
- Elena: customer impact notes + 3 case studies to use in comms (due: 2026-07-26)
- Marcus: finalize slide skeleton and distribute pre-read (due: 2026-07-22)

Notes & tone guidance for the talk (short):
- Be explicit about tradeoffs; people accept tradeoffs if rationale is clear
- Reinforce the theme: "serve predictably and efficiently" — keep that phrase
- Surface wins but avoid overpromising on timelines

Appendix (handy links):
- Pre-read metrics sheet: link in linked_artifacts
- Current OKRs doc: confluence:OKR-2026-Q3

Bottom line (TL;DR):
We recommend adopting Option A (Focused efficiency) as the primary company-level OKR pivot for Q4, with a small set of org-specific stretch OKRs for growth experiments. Keep communication short, call out owners, and lock the decisions in the decision log during Day 3 synthesis.

---
Draft status: rough. Expect edits in the exec alignment meeting; use this file as the canonical ephemeral record for the reset week.

"Notes to self: if we get pushback on batching thresholds, have fallback: temporary increased capacity + canary rollout for latency-sensitive routes."
